passages.title: Interview with a young chef
passages.text: Interviewer: Today we are joined by Maya, a 22-year-old chef who recently opened her first restaurant. Maya, was it always your dream to cook professionally? Maya: Honestly, no. I studied graphic design first! But I spent all my free time helping my grandmother in her kitchen. I realized that the pressure of a busy service was actually where I felt most alive. Interviewer: Many people find the long hours in a kitchen difficult. How do you manage? Maya: It is exhausting, I won't lie. You are on your feet for twelve hours. But I have a great team, and we support each other. If I didn't love the creativity of inventing new dishes, I would have quit months ago. Interviewer: What is the most challenging part of your job? Maya: People think it's the cooking, but it's actually the management. Ordering ingredients, dealing with staff, and keeping the budget in check—that's the real work. The cooking is the reward at the end of the day. Interviewer: Do you have advice for young people wanting to enter the industry? Maya: Don't expect to be a head chef immediately. Start at the bottom, learn how to clean, how to prep, and be humble. You need to be willing to fail a few times before you get it right.

questions.question: Why did Maya decide to become a chef?
questions.explanation: Maya explains that she realized she enjoyed the busy atmosphere of a kitchen more than her original studies.
options: a) She discovered she loved the pressure of the kitchen environment.
b) She wanted to follow in her grandmother's footsteps.
c) She failed her graphic design course.

questions.question: What does Maya say helps her deal with the long working hours?
questions.explanation: Maya mentions that having a supportive team and the creative aspect of the job keeps her going.
options: a) She enjoys the creative side of inventing new recipes.
b) She plans to reduce her hours once the restaurant is successful.
c) She takes frequent breaks throughout the day.

questions.question: According to Maya, what is the most difficult part of her job?
questions.explanation: She clarifies that the business and management side is more challenging than the actual cooking.
options: a) Preparing the ingredients for the day.
b) Managing the business and staff responsibilities.
c) Creating new dishes for the menu.

questions.question: What advice does Maya give to aspiring chefs?
questions.explanation: She advises starting at the bottom and being humble, rather than expecting immediate high positions.
options: a) They should avoid working in busy kitchens at first.
b) They should focus on being creative from the start.
c) They should be prepared to do basic tasks first.
